reason: Checked against the source. sky_check has one caller (sky.6502 .fresh, after geom with d1 = sky_jl, d2 = sky_jh), and the whole-row path is reached only when sky_row returns Z set, i.e. sky_rn = 8. sky_geom (sky_hazel.6502) gives rn = 8 only with rt = 7: the bottom row when L = 7, the middle and top rows (which store rt = 7), and the cross entry, which copies rt and rn. sky_ry is always a multiple of 8: ytop = 8*(d2-d1); the cross entry's values come from rl, which is 8*d1 + (A AND &F8) - 8, minus &80 for each row above, so also a multiple of 8. So Y = 8k+7. With d2-d1 <= 13 (a 14-column image block) Y <= 111, and the unrolled loop never starts at Y >= 128, which is the one case where it would read 7 extra bytes. It reads the same bytes in the same order and leaves A = their OR, Y = &FF and N set, as before. TAX then BEQ next_row / BRA dirty go to the same targets, and nothing at either target reads A or Y (next_row reloads X from sky_q). The reads go through (s_ptr),Y as before, with the same paging (bank 4, renderer, ACCCON) and the same addresses. It touches no PROTECTED or generated line, no table and no zero page. It is not raster-timed, beyond being faster. Room: +21 bytes in bank 4, under REN_BASE. Built in a scratch copy: the shipping build, make gameplay, SKY_HELI=2 with DEBUG_LIVES, and the gameplay flags with SKY_HELI=2 all assemble. The SHIFT=256 bench build fails with 'bank 5 overruns by 239', and HEAD fails the same way, so this change did not cause it. Shipping: .full at &A330, BPL full at &A348 (no page crossing). Gameplay: &A164 to &A17C. Cycles: the old loop is 10 a byte (ORA 5, DEY 2, BPL 3), the new one 59 a pass of 8 bytes, which saves 21 a pass, so 21*(k+1). The clean exit saves 2 more (BEQ taken, 3, against BNE 2 + BRA 3); the dirty exit costs 2 more. For k = 11 (a 12-column rectangle) that is 254, close to the claimed 258. Bytes: 12 become 33, +21 as claimed.
